provenance.review_metadata_caveat: Resolved/unresolved/outdated thread metadata does not prove current code passes or fails. Decisions above derive from pinned actual source. Discussion URLs are reviewer-question traceability, not runtime evidence.
provenance.inspection: Pinned source reads, exact line checks and Git blob/tree metadata only. Comparison is source-only; no simulator builds/runs or production edits performed. No pushes or official repository mutations.
provenance.confidence_limit: High confidence for cited source behavior/declarations. No new runtime or physical-power accuracy qualification; test source presence does not mean tests passed.

decisions.area: Shared parser and direct cluster factory
decisions.finding: Current PR already embeds the normalized workload reader and directly constructs SimObjects. Its native path does not require per-benchmark generated Python. Paths are relative to the declaring YAML and recursive SysPath includes reject.
decisions.dependency_change_impact: Adopt this architecture with an adapter for current workbench YAML, leaf IR paths, class names and address allocation; schema compatibility is not automatic.
decisions.preserved_invariants: Every accepted field has an active consumer or a pre-instantiation error; source/effective input identities stay recorded.
decisions.required_validation: Roundtrip current GEMM YAML; unknown-field/missing/include-cycle negatives; inspect config.ini and independently check numeric output.

decisions.finding: PR SALAMArmBoard uses ArmFsWorkload, explicit ELF setter and direct attachment. It requires a classic hierarchy exposing membus and bypasses Linux-specific ArmBoard pre-instantiation setup.
decisions.dependency_change_impact: Add a separate native GEMM route using current engine first. The lifecycle override is version-sensitive; validate against pinned develop. Keep legacy runner available.
decisions.preserved_invariants: Fixed CPU/single system scope; same ELF/exit transport/independent output checks; qualified checkpoint untouched.
decisions.required_validation: Actual board instantiate and config.ini wiring, clocks, ELF; real seeded GEMM plus deliberate corruption; final scalar override precedence.

decisions.area: Single profile data module and SCons dependency graph
decisions.finding: PR generates only _salam_profile.py, declares config/instruction/FU/generator/power-parser inputs and embeds data in the variant build. This is a cleaner target than our generated typed wrapper graph and temporary text patching.
decisions.dependency_change_impact: Adopt variant-local declared generation, coupled to A04 generic ABI conversion. Do not remove wrapper outputs while C++ includes require them. This exact PR still selects profile data at build time; it is not unrestricted hot reload.
decisions.preserved_invariants: Determinism, content hashes, rebuild provenance and capability checks; fractional PPA stays floating point.
decisions.required_validation: Clean/out-of-tree build; edit every input category and verify rebuild; isolated profiles do not contaminate; unchanged input stable.

decisions.finding: PR uses generic FunctionalUnit/InstructionConfig entries with vector Params and camelCase getters. Ours uses FunctionalUnitBase/InstConfigBase, generated typed members and snake_case getters. Upstream Python data objects alone cannot satisfy our C++ ABI.
decisions.dependency_change_impact: Own C++ changes: generic entries/constructors, vectors/ownership, lookup/getter adaptation, HWInterface Params/includes, LLVMInterface iteration and SCons. Preserve scheduler semantics; retire old wrapper dependency graph only after no consumers remain.
decisions.preserved_invariants: Unknown/duplicate ID rejection; opcode mapping; no live occupancy at start/end; complete FU trace/replay.
decisions.required_validation: Pure mapping/accessor fixtures then actual SimObject ownership/config.ini, old/new GEMM numeric and trace parity, finite/unlimited sweeps.

decisions.finding: Actual PR C++ resolves limit=0 to one instance per reachable static instruction and uses that finite pool. Our pool treats limit=0 as no occupancy cap. This is a scheduling change, not configuration cleanup.
decisions.dependency_change_impact: Reject implicit replacement. Keep unlimited=0 for existing profiles. A future static_graph sizing mode needs a named policy and schema migration.
decisions.preserved_invariants: Finite/unlimited behavior; per-instruction cap=0 means no extra requested cap, not exemption from a finite FU cap.
decisions.required_validation: Caps 0/1/2/4 with enough ready dynamic operations to distinguish static sizing from unlimited; independent complete lease replay with zero outstanding.

decisions.finding: PR pool assigns per-instance nextIssue and allows overlap for interval>0; zero is unpipelined. Our current pool is nonpipelined occupancy capacity. PR YAML omits interval to mean zero; explicit interval must be >=1.
decisions.dependency_change_impact: Defer until native configuration parity. Requires per-instance accounting, tick conversion, completion leases and richer independent replay.
decisions.preserved_invariants: Logging budget never changes scheduling; throughput separated from operation latency; grant/deny/release audit retained.
decisions.required_validation: Long-latency overlap microkernel; expected admission ticks for intervals 1/2 and unpipelined; overflow and relaunch controls.

decisions.finding: Both engines execute instruction latency from CycleCounts. PR labels FU stages/cycles/datatype fields descriptive and rejects obsolete instruction-profile runtime_cycles/functional_unit_limit. Workload runtime_cycles remains active. Our existing _apply_cycle_counts path is active.
decisions.dependency_change_impact: Adopt one latency path with honest labels; move active legacy runtime cycles into workload overrides; remove only redundant generated storage; reject unsupported nonzero instruction caps; preserve name normalization.
decisions.preserved_invariants: GUI latency reaches actual CycleCounts; descriptive metadata is not presented as execution control.
decisions.required_validation: Latency sweep changes real issue/completion ticks while numeric output stays equal; reject unsupported nonzero memory/immediate-terminator latencies.

decisions.area: Native compute/fabric clocks and final overrides
decisions.finding: PR creates Compute/Fabric native domains and binds accelerator versus local bus/DMA/memory; compute scheduling uses clockEdge. Our native engine already uses clockEdge but requires retained integer-ns clock_period to match clk_domain after final scalar overrides.
decisions.dependency_change_impact: Adapt direct native domains while reconciling legacy clocks only after scalar overrides. First slice keeps integer-ns constraints; arbitrary frequencies need replacing our constructor checks in LLVMInterface/CommInterface/DMA and separate qualification.
decisions.preserved_invariants: Edge alignment and no duplicate same-edge pass; independent actor clocks; reset semantics; CPU switching/distributed roots remain unqualified.
decisions.required_validation: Existing 10/3 ns plus nonaligned launches; independent Compute/Fabric sweeps; config.ini; conflicting override negatives; repeated launches around native reset.

decisions.finding: PR has source JSON, implementation IDs, signatures, physical units/geometry and incomplete-coverage policy for PPA accounting. Our SALAMPowerModel C++ is an empty constructor; legacy coefficients elsewhere are not an interchangeable calibrated model.
decisions.dependency_change_impact: Defer full migration after configuration/FU parity. Adopt units/provenance/coverage vocabulary; never turn legacy configured coefficients into calibrated results by renaming. C++ event accounting, memory observers and inventory are required.
decisions.preserved_invariants: Unknown is not zero; configured uncalibrated coefficients remain labeled; observer cannot change numerical execution.
decisions.required_validation: Synthetic energy ledger; missing/mixed units/geometry negatives; observer enabled/disabled execution parity; source hashes/coverage visible.

decisions.finding: Ours explicitly checks LLVM major 14 and typed-pointer IR. PR lists LLVM 11-20 for suffixed executable discovery, but explicit LLVM_CONFIG or PATH llvm-config is not major-version checked by configure_llvm_for_salam. Link flags/ABI-disable macros do not prove our engine supports that range.
decisions.dependency_change_impact: Reject blanket version broadening and LLVM_DISABLE_ABI_BREAKING_CHECKS_ENFORCING transplant. Keep optional LLVM14 gate until each toolchain/IR is tested. PR DataLayout handling is promising but spans value/register/GEP/cast/comparison semantics, not a header-only import.
decisions.preserved_invariants: Ordinary gem5 has no LLVM dependency; actionable wrong/missing version errors; gem5 compiler/exception policy preserved; unsupported types fail closed.
decisions.required_validation: Non-SALAM build without LLVM; missing/wrong LLVM negatives; exact executable/version/link flags recorded; compiler/IR/pointer/type/address-space matrix.

decisions.area: Unsupported IR rejected in actual engine
decisions.finding: PR rejects atomics including atomic load/store and FenceInst before opcode dispatch, and rejects recursion while constructing graph. Ours has explicit unsupported-opcode fatal, but atomic load/store use ordinary Load/Store opcodes and are not rejected by that switch alone.
decisions.dependency_change_impact: Plan own C++ pre-dispatch atomic/Fence rejection and explicit bounded recursion checks; compare existing unconditional CFG guard before transplant. Workbench preflight supplements, not substitutes for, native boundary checks. No implementation in this audit.
decisions.preserved_invariants: Actual simulator negative modules exit nonzero with IR context; rejected IR cannot proceed to numeric oracle.
decisions.required_validation: Assembler-valid atomic load/store/RMW/cmpxchg/fence; direct/indirect recursion policy; unsupported scalar/vector/aggregate modules through native and GUI routes.

decisions.area: Native metrics and direct invocation evidence
decisions.finding: PR has execution/per-unit native stats and quiescence assertion. Ours additionally emits invocation JSON/full FU JSON and resettable completedInvocations/invocationTicks. Whole-file engine replacement would change observable contracts.
decisions.dependency_change_impact: Adapt native stats patterns without losing direct JSON/replay contract. Keep pass counts distinct from elapsed duration, tick-weighted averages distinct from pass-sampled ones, and specify native-reset versus invocation-file lifetime.
decisions.preserved_invariants: No output-banner-only pass; no overwritten invocation files; zero outstanding leases; reset does not erase independent invocation evidence.
decisions.required_validation: Two launches with native reset; reconcile full numeric output, JSON/native complete/tick counters and independent FU replay; truncation explicit.

decisions.finding: Our response helper pins blocked/in-callback heads and avoids iterator underflow; CommInterface snapshots packet direction before ownership transfer. Both engines explicitly release graph edges on finalize. Front-end migration does not justify whole-engine/device overwrite.
decisions.dependency_change_impact: Reject wholesale engine/device replacement. Review upstream hunks separately with behavior tests; preserve queue, float conversion, clock-overflow and teardown repairs. Helper tests do not prove all real SimObject backpressure/drain cases.
decisions.preserved_invariants: Response ordering, retry/callback packet lifetime, bounded float conversion/clock guards, fresh graph per invocation.
decisions.required_validation: Helper regressions plus actual SimObject forced request/response backpressure, synchronous callbacks and bypass/drain/lifetime cases as separate gates.

decisions.finding: PR contains TestLib suites, board wiring assertions and expected-suite checker rejecting missing/skipped/zero tests. Source presence is useful design evidence, not proof these tests passed in this audit or with our engine.
decisions.dependency_change_impact: Adopt suite/results reconciliation and actual board config assertions alongside independent numerical/negative workbench checks. Label helper/SimObject/full-simulation evidence separately; custom profiles require isolated builds/default restoration.
decisions.preserved_invariants: No passing zero-test run; exact binary/source/profile identity; source-only findings never upgrade runtime qualification.
decisions.required_validation: Enumerate expected IDs; run bounded suites then reconcile XML; injected missing-suite/incorrect-output controls fail.

minimal_native_gemm_route.details: First slice keeps current generated FU/instruction ABI and LLVM14 gate. Normalize GEMM workload, profile references, addresses/ports, leaf IR and actor clocks. Every accepted field maps to a consumer or rejects.

Use PR parser/factory organization but create our current CommInterface, LLVMInterface, HWInterface, CycleCounts, FunctionalUnits, HWStatistics, InstConfig, InstOpCodes, SALAMPowerModel and SimulatorConfig children. Match existing wiring/address/IR contracts. Fixed compiled unit set initially; new arbitrary units need later ABI migration.

Adapt board pattern with explicit ELF, classic cache/membus/GIC and final override-to-clock reconciliation. Keep old runner. No C++ rewrite is intrinsically needed for existing typed objects, supported scalar IR and integer-ns clocks.

minimal_native_gemm_route.task: Qualify real parity before generic conversion
minimal_native_gemm_route.details: Old and direct routes: same seeded GEMM, independent full output and deliberate corruption, config.ini mapping, caps 0/1/2/4, latency sweep, 10/3 ns clocks, two launches/native reset, direct/native metrics and full FU lease replay.

minimal_native_gemm_route.task: Convert generic Params and declared profile generation
minimal_native_gemm_route.details: Then own C++/Params/header/SCons conversion A03/A04 without static-count zero or new initiation intervals; preserve trace/native stats. Only retire legacy dependency graph after complete consumer search and explicit compatibility decision.
Atomic/recursion engine fail-closed hardening, pipeline intervals, static sizing, arbitrary clocks, LLVM expansion and characterized PPA each need separately declared semantics and tests.

own_cpp_change_plan.required: No intrinsic C++ changes for factory restricted to existing compiled typed objects, supported LLVM14 scalar IR and integer-ns clocks; existing required children and scalar/domain checks must be satisfied.
Generic FU/instruction entries, constructors/vector ownership, HWInterface Params/includes/getters, LLVMInterface iteration/lookup, SCons registration; preserve scheduling/JSON/stats.
Pre-dispatch atomic load/store/Fence rejection and explicit bounded recursion handling in llvm_interface.cc.
Per-instance initiation interval and independent replay; optional named static-graph sizing; replacement of legacy actor clock consistency checks for arbitrary frequency support.
DataLayout-aware value/register/GEP/cast/comparison handling and tested compiler/IR matrix before widening LLVM versions.

clean_upstream_candidate_scope.method: Fresh candidate on pinned upstream develop; no whole-fork or whole-PR merge.
first_slice_include: optional SALAM opt-in registration and bounded LLVM14 dependency handling
required compute/communications/memory engine and correctness helpers
CycleCounts/FU/InstConfig/HWInterface dependencies required by that engine
native Group metrics and bounded test-visible observation/replay contract
one direct parser/factory and bare-metal native GEMM example
small deterministic workload and numerical/negative TestLib fixtures
keep_external_or_defer: Workbench GUI/server/report packaging remains in user fork initially
full benchmark corpus, historical experiments and generated outputs
legacy generated-code front ends unless a documented transition needs them
physical PPA migration, initiation intervals and static-graph zero sizing
reviewer_questions: Does ordinary gem5 build and run without LLVM or SALAM imports?
Can native GEMM run without checkout-specific sys.path/import/generated-module assumptions?
Do all accepted settings reach active consumers or fail explicitly?
Are workloads deterministic, licensed, small and covered by expected-suite reconciliation?
Are native stats reset/units/lifetime and port/retry/drain responsibilities documented?
clean_upstream_candidate_scope.notice: Preserve source attribution and every required license/copyright notice. Do not infer new ownership. Scope is a proposal, not approval to delete legacy code.
